title: Feeling Faces

serves.summary: The child drags feeling faces (happy, sad, mad, scared, surprised, worried) onto children in a picture, matching a spoken feeling word to its face and reading from a situation (a dropped ice cream, a dog running up) how each child feels, including two children who feel differently about the same thing, which shows understanding of words for feelings.

request.topic: Feeling words: matching a feeling to a face and to what caused it
request.objective: Match a feeling word to the face that shows it, and a situation to the face of the child in it, including two children who feel differently about the same thing. (LA005-01-G, LA006-02-A)

problems.ask: This child feels sad. Give the child the sad face.
problems.goal: The sad face on the child. The happy face is the miss.

props.name: ice cream fallen on the ground, melting

problems.ask: Oh no! This child dropped their ice cream. Give the child a face that shows how they feel.
problems.goal: A sad or a mad face (both fit losing the ice cream). The happy face, chosen because ice cream is a happy thing, is the miss.
